rationale: The candidate reads coherently across views as a single split-wing mass, so gesture and hierarchy are present, but the form remains too box-like and weakly sectioned for the neighborhood-living brief. The visible split does not yet become a meaningful public void or terrace; it reads more like a small gap between two blocks than a usable ground threshold. The blue access edge is not convincingly answered by a public seam, notch, or open court, so the frontage relation is still semantically weak. Compared with the references, it has some affinity to compact commercial massing, but it does not yet carry the strong courtyard/public-space logic of the similar precedents or the sectional continuity of the counterfactual. Program-fit therefore fails because the mass does not visibly support an active ground edge plus one clear public void/terrace and calm upper hierarchy.
